method: Second round. Read scope/taxpapers-result.json (every row, its recheck lists and mutation records) against final-checks/zzzz-scope-taxpapers.json; tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts in full; git diff of statetax.ts (stateDueOf, stateAccrual monthly rounding, stateNextNotice, statePlanRefusal), taxreturn.ts (armCollection, stateDueOf callers), PapersWorkspace.tsx, lending.ts, health.ts (for new income writers), guide/taxes.ts, guide/papers.ts, guide/money.ts and tutorial.ts. Ran tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts alone: 17 passed. Probe (scratchpad/probe/nowage.probe.ts): London-born lives of all six families with their money in a CD from creation still buy the PPE and work, each with $1,656.00 of work-study in 2026 (wealthy and inherited too). Nothing in the repository was edited; no mutation was run (the result's mutation records were checked by reasoning against the assertions).

rows.disposition: All four of round one's problems are closed. A plan ended paid by Pay is now played (test :372; the <=0 to <0 mutation turns status 'paid' into 'active'). The rounding fix is real (stateAccrual rounds each month's 1%), and $649.71, $655.56, $661.41 and $17.55 are worked from 12-735. A levy is now shown pending before the payment (:338). Connecticut's April date on a 1040-NR comes from stateDueOf and is tested by TEST SETUP. Reverting it moves the pending bill to 15 July, so the test fails.
problems: tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts:539-542 and the result's recheck give the TEST SETUP's reason as 'Yale's work-study is paid on the clock to every student with need'. That is wrong. The Wealthy family, with no need and no scholarship, has the same $1,656.00 (:608, and the probe: all six families). Assigned shifts can be missed by play: away from New Haven, a sick day, PPE the bank can't cover, or not registered (src/engine/systems/school.ts:3127-3172). So a wage-free 1040-NR is not shown unreachable. The conclusion still survives for 2026 in substance: the scholarship alone, $14,014.00, is under Connecticut's $15,000 exemption, worked back from $3.35 = 25% of 2% of $670. So no Connecticut balance arises. 2027 isn't argued.

Minor display gap. On a 1040-NR without wages, Papers shows the return as 'Due' r.due, 15 June (src/ui/workspaces/PapersWorkspace.tsx:465), and No Returns Yet gives 15 June (:424), with no word that Connecticut's side runs from mid-April. Only the tutorial and the guide say so. The tutorial line (src/engine/content/tutorial.ts:276, 'File It by mid-April, or by June 15 on a 1040-NR with no wages on it, though Connecticut’s return on it is still due in mid-April.') is true of the code. stateDueOf gives Connecticut's penalty, interest, bill, non-filer notice and plan refusal the resident deadline. Connecticut has no file-late penalty (fileLate monthly 0), so filing late costs its 10% and 1% a month only where something is owed.

src/engine/content/guide/taxes.ts:196 and :246 say Connecticut's bill and levy come 'after the deadline'. On a 1040-NR due in June, 'the deadline' could be read as 15 June. The Penalty row (:269) says mid-April, so this is ambiguous, not false.
weakTests: a 1040-NR’s 15 June is the IRS’s alone … (TEST SETUP of r.due; its stated reason for the setup is inaccurate, see problems)
